title: Adaptive Goal Sherpa — Personal KPI Notebook
content:
Context: quick, practical notebook I use to keep weekly momentum on small wins + measurable improvements. Not a polished PRD — think scratchpad + micro-OKRs + action log.

Why 'Sherpa'? The idea is a guiding process: help me carry load, point safe routes, nudge on cadence. Focus is on throughput improvements for my projects (serving-runtime), but also sustainable habits so I don't burn out.

Monthly northstar (Jan-Feb 2025):
- Improve model-serving PR merge-to-deploy lead time by 25% (baseline = 6.4 days).
- Reduce on-call jolts from infra regressions to <= 2 incidents/month.
- Ship 3 docs/mini-guides for new joiners about cache/kv best practices.

Success metrics I track weekly (personal dashboard):
- Focus hours (deep work blocks logged): target 18/week.
- PRs merged that I authored: >= 3/week (small fixes count).
- Mentoring sessions: >= 1/week (pair debugging, onboarding).
- Customer escalations triaged (handed back to SRE/CS): <= 2/month.
- Oddly important: number of times I unblock someone within 24h (aim 5+/wk).

Current baseline snapshot (week of 2025-02-10):
- Focus hours: 12 (missed due to ops fire + onboarding syncs).
- PR lead time (my PRs): median 4.8 days (good), overall team lead time: 5.3 days.
- On-call jolts this month: 1 (pgbouncer regression, mitigated).
- Docs written: 1 draft (cache-kv-quickstart).

Weekly cadence (how I actually run check-ins):
- Monday AM: 15–20m quick plan — top 3 outcomes for the week (pin them).
- Wed noon: 10m mid-week triage — cancel or move items; call out blockers.
- Friday: 25–30m retrospective + backlog tidy (what shipped, what stuck, 1 experiment to try next week).

This week's top 3 outcomes (Wk 7, target dates 2025-02-10 -> 2025-02-16):
1) Finish cache-kv quickstart doc + circulate to infra-council (w/ checklist and example tracing).
2) Reduce PR review latency by nudging reviewers with a /review-please script and pairing 1 hour block.
3) Run focused experiment on batching config for Llama-like models on p4d pool (collect perf + cost delta).

Action plan & micro-tasks (status tags: TODO | IN_PROGRESS | BLOCKED | DONE):
- TODO: Outline cache-kv quickstart (headers + examples) — ETA Tue 2/11 — notes in doc 'cache-kv-quickstart'.
- IN_PROGRESS: Implement /review-please bot script (proof-of-concept in my fork) — linked PR above.
- TODO: Schedule 1-hour pairing with Jon to unblock kernel selection decisions — propose Thu 2/13 10am.
- BLOCKED: Perf logs from p4d run (need S3 path from infra ops) — pinged #infra-ops (Eliot).
- TODO: Add small checklist for oncall runbooks to reduce cognitive load during incidents.

Mini-experiments (hypotheses + measurement plan):
1) Hypothesis: Short, labeled pairing sessions cut reviewer latency by 30% for critical PRs.
   - Measure: reviewer-first-response time for PRs with pairing tag vs control.
   - Experiment window: 2 weeks.
2) Hypothesis: 30m deep-work before 11am increases weekly focus hours by 15%.
   - Measure: log of blocked calendar time + subjective midweek score (1-5).
   - Tweak: If not effective, try morning + evening split.
3) Hypothesis: A tiny doc (1 page) reduces repeat oncall questions by 40%.
   - Measure: repeat question count in #sre-questions thread with doc link.

Retrospective notes (last 2 weeks):
- What went well: triaged pgbouncer regression quickly; used checklist from previous incident which saved ~45m. Finished one mentoring session that led to two merged bugfixes.
- What was frustrating: too many shallow meetings, granularity of PR reviews varied — need stronger PR description templates.
- Decide: enforce PR template for serving-runtime (minimal repro steps + perf baseline). Create a small PR template and link to it in the quickstart doc.

Risks & blockers:
- If infra ops can't surface perf logs quickly, batching experiment stalls. Mitigation: temporary local simulation + small sample traces.
- Oncall fatigue creeping up if we don't rotate more predictably — talk to manager about swap cadence.

Notes to self (raw, unedited):
- Stop checking Slack in first 60m; calendar block will be a test.
- Micro-tracker: mark 4x 45m deep blocks per week in calendar.
- If more than 3 context switches/day, flag day as low-velocity and reduce new commitments.

Follow-ups (next 7 days):
- Send cache-kv quickstart draft to infra-council (Eliot, Sasha) — Tue 2/11.
- Run p4d mini-batch test, capture perf and cost numbers — Wed 2/12.
- Ship /review-please v0.1 — Fri 2/14 and monitor reviewer latency for 1 week.
- Update PR template and add short checklist to PR description — Fri 2/14.

Quick links & references I keep here:
- Short internal checklist for incidents: confluence.redwood.internal/incident-mini-checklist
- PR template note (draft): github.com/redwood-inference/serving-runtime/.github/pull_request_template.md
- Oncall rotation notes: /team/eng-serving-runtime/schedules (linked in calendar)

Unresolved questions (for manager sync):
- Can we get a recurring 2-hour blocked window for deep work on Tue mornings for the serving-runtime team? If yes, trial for one month.
- Is there appetite to formalize the pairing hour as an official 'review office hour' per sprint?

End-of-note quick mood/energy ticker (subjective):
- Energy: 3/5 (wore thin over last sprint)
- Focus: 2/5 (ops interruptions)

Tiny personal rules (Sherpa commandments):
- Carry the map, not the whole pack: document small, actionable steps rather than massive essays.
- When in doubt, pair for 1 hour.
- Ship a 1-pager before a 10-pager.

-- marta
